newsitem.title: USA: Religious group seeks to aid poultry workers.
newsitem.headline: Religious group seeks to aid poultry workers.

text.p: A group of religious leaders said Monday it would work to improve wages, benefits and conditions for 240,000 workers in the nation's poultry processing industry.
Leaders of the Chicago-based National Interfaith Committee for Worker Justice said at a news conference that immigrant workers were often mistreated at poultry processing plants.
The committee said immigrant workers received poor wages and benefits and risked repetitive motion injuries such as carpal tunnel syndrome because of the high speed of processing lines.
"When I tell people what's going on, they're shocked," said executive director Kim Bobo.
Singled out for criticism was a poultry processing plant in Morganton, N. C., where Guatemalan immigrant workers went on an eight-day strike last month.
Workers from the plant said their restroom breaks were limited and they had to buy their own safety equipment, including gloves and boots, at inflated prices.
Labour leaders said the workers were crammed into small trailers with no air conditioning or heating and charged as much as $1,000 per month in rent.
The executive board of the National Interfaith Committee for Worker Justice includes national leaders from 18 denominations, orders and faith communities.
